title: Quote Anchoring Probe Benchmark
body:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a compact, reviewable probe benchmark and acceptance criteria for onboarding LLM variants into RAG pipelines where quote fidelity and grounding are first-class requirements. The suite is optimized for: quote accuracy (literal reproduction of quoted spans), explicit source anchoring (URL/id and span), and correct refusal when the answer cannot be grounded in provided context.

Scope and motivation:
- Focus: model outputs that return quoted text from retrieved sources (news, docs, user manuals). We test literal quote fidelity and whether the model invents or hallucinates attributions.
- Intended usage: applied-ml onboarding flow (smoke -> regression -> canary -> rollout). Lightweight manual sampling plus automated checks.
- Not in scope: deep semantic summarization quality (separate eval).

High-level acceptance criteria (per-check):
1) Exact-quote fidelity: when prompt asks to "quote exactly" a target sentence present in context, model must reproduce >= 95% token overlap with the ground-truth quote (normalized whitespace and punctuation).
2) Anchor presence: when asked for a source, model must include either the document id, canonical URL, or a 1–3 token identifier matched to retrieval metadata. Required in >= 98% of positive cases.
3) Refusal behavior: when context does not contain answer text, model must return a concise refusal (e.g. "I cannot find a quote for that in the supplied sources") in >= 99% of negative cases and avoid fabricating quotes.
4) Hallucination cap: measured hallucinated-quote rate <= 1% across the full test battery.

Test battery structure (components):
- Positive exact-match cases (40 prompts): single-span quotes, verbatim reproduction expected.
- Positive paraphrase cases (20 prompts): model should indicate paraphrase vs quote; if asked for a quote, should refuse and optionally offer a paraphrase section clearly labeled.
- Negative/no-evidence cases (30 prompts): question not answerable from provided snippets; expect refusal.
- Conflicting-sources cases (20 prompts): two retrieved snippets with different quoted variants; expect the model to present both variants with explicit source anchors and to avoid combining them into a new fused quote.
- Partial-span cases (20 prompts): context contains only part of the target sentence; expect refusal to quote but allow to indicate partial match with exact span metadata.
- Long-form extraction (10 prompts): multi-sentence quoted passages — test token-overlap across longer spans.

Example test cases (representative excerpts):
1) Positive exact-match (news):
- Prompt: "From the provided articles, quote verbatim the sentence that starts with 'The committee concluded' and include the source URL."
- Context: article snippet includes "The committee concluded that further study was needed, citing budget constraints."
- Expected: quote exactly: "The committee concluded that further study was needed, citing budget constraints." plus URL and a span reference.
- Accept if token overlap >= 95% after normalization.

2) Negative / no evidence:
- Prompt: "Quote the sentence that claims the company filed for bankruptcy on 2023-09-18."
- Context: retrieved docs do not mention bankruptcy.
- Expected: a refusal line (one or two sentences) and an optional suggestion to re-run retrieval with broader scope.

3) Conflicting sources:
- Prompt: "Provide the exact quote that mentions the 'primary driver' and indicate which source it came from."
- Context: Source A: "The primary driver was identified as supply-chain delays." Source B: "The primary driver was identified as regulatory uncertainty."
- Expected: list both quotes separately with their source IDs; no invented reconciliation sentence like "primary driver included supply-chain delays and regulatory uncertainty" as a single quoted span.

Scoring rubric (automated and manual):
- QuoteF1 (automated): token-level F1 between predicted quote and ground-truth quote after normalization (lowercase, strip excess whitespace, unify Unicode).
- Anchor-Precision: fraction of outputs that include a valid anchor (matches retrieval metadata).
- Refusal-Recall: fraction of negative cases where the model properly refused.
- Hallucination-rate: fraction of outputs containing tokens/phrases not present in any retrieved source when the output claims a source.
- Manual review signal: for any failing batch where QuoteF1 < 0.8 or Hallucination-rate > 0.02, select 200 samples for human annotation.

Automated harness notes (implementation pointers):
- Use the existing rag-eval-harness repo as the driver; add a QuoteAnchoring task type with fields: prompt_template_id, retrieval_ids, target_span_offsets, expected_quote.
- Postprocess outputs: extract first quoted span (heuristic: text between quotation marks), fallback to span matching by longest common substring if quotes aren't used.
- Metadata checks: validate that reported anchor id matches one of retrieval_ids. If model provides natural language anchors (e.g., "article 3"), compare normalized label mapping generated at retrieval-time.

Regression thresholds and alerts:
- Canary threshold: compared to baseline model (current prod), new model should not regress by more than 2 ppt on Anchor-Precision and 3 ppt on QuoteF1 on a 5k-sample canary.
- Blocking regression: +5 ppt regression in Hallucination-rate or QuoteF1 drop > 6 ppt triggers rollback.
- Alerting: failures open JIRA-AIENG-4127 with an auto-attached failure CSV and sample outputs.

Manual review process:
- Sampling: stratified by case type (exact, paraphrase, conflict, negative) — default N=50 per stratum.
- Annotation guide: annotators mark (A) quote exactness, (B) anchor correctness, (C) hallucination presence, (D) correct refusal. Use binary flags plus free-text notes.
- Inter-rater agreement: require Cohen's kappa >= 0.6 across dual annotated batches; if below, run calibration session.

Known failure modes and mitigations:
- Model paraphrases instead of quoting: add explicit instruction tokens and a short prefix "Quote exactly - do not paraphrase"; consider temperature=0 for deterministic decoding in canary.
- Fused quotes from multiple sources: require that any quoted span must match a single retrieval span; update postprocess to detect multi-source provenance and mark as invalid.
- Partial matches accepted as full quotes: add checks for exact substring match and enforce minimum overlap thresholds.
- Anchors omitted or paraphrased: apply a soft penalty in scoring and add a tied prompt slot where an explicit anchor is requested ("Include the document URL or ID after the quote").

Privacy and provenance concerns:
- Test data should not contain PII. Use synthetic or sanitized public-source excerpts for test samples.
- Record retrieval ids and canonical URLs in the test harness but mask any internal access tokens in artifacts.

Smoke checklist before release to canary:
- Run full battery on baseline model and new model; compare metrics and capture diffs.
- Confirm harness extracts quoted spans correctly on a developer sample of 200 prompts.
- Verify JIRA integration and output CSV formatting.
- Run manual annotation on 300 stratified samples.

Rollout recommendations:
- Canary: 5% traffic for two days with continuous monitoring (per-minute Hallucination-rate, Anchor-Precision).
- Ramp: 25% for 24 hours if no alarming regressions, then 50% then 100% across 72 hour windows.

Next steps / TODOs (owner assignments):
- [Lena] finalize the 140-item test bank and upload to rag-eval-harness test vectors.
- [Rajiv] implement QuoteAnchoring task type and postprocessing heuristics.
- [Maya] curate sanitized sources and generate negative/no-evidence cases.
- [Theo] add Canary dashboards and alert hooks in Grafana.

Notes / open questions:
- How to handle canonicalization for newswire where retrieval returns syndicated duplicates? (proposed: prefer canonical URL mapping table).
- Should paraphrase cases be scored separately with a label "paraphrase okay"? Propose a dual-track scoring: QuoteF1 (strict) + ParaphraseAgree (semantic match).

Appendix: sample prompts (quick copy-paste)
- "Quote verbatim any sentence that contains the phrase 'policy shift' from the supplied sources, and append the source id."
- "If there is no verbatim sentence that mentions 'percentage growth', say 'No quote found in supplied sources.' Do not guess."
- "List exact sentences that mention 'primary safety concern' and tag each with the source filename or URL. If multiple sources disagree, list each sentence and source separately."

This document is intentionally concise and operational — meant to live in Drive as the working spec for the quote-anchoring eval. Feedback requested from applied-ml reviewers and solutions-engineering for edge-case prompts.
